findings.summary: Ableton Live is a digital audio workstation for macOS and Windows designed as a live performance instrument and production tool. It uses two interface views: Session View for launching clips and scenes in real time, and Arrangement View for linear timeline editing and MIDI sequencing. The software handles audio via Warping for time-stretching and pitch-preserving tempo adjustment, and supports MIDI to trigger built-in and third-party instruments. Three main editions exist—Intro, Standard, and Suite—with Suite including Max for Live. Lite is a limited version bundled with hardware. The software originated in the mid-1990s from Berlin-based developers who prototyped features in Max, and it expanded from live-looping to full DAW functionality with VST support in 2004.

mechanisms.title: Dual-View Architecture
mechanisms.explanation: Live's interface splits into Session View, a grid for triggering clips and scenes in any order suitable for performance, and Arrangement View, a horizontal timeline for linear recording, editing, and MIDI sequencing. Clips launched in Session View can be recorded into Arrangement View for further manipulation.

mechanisms.title: Warping Time-Stretching
mechanisms.explanation: Live's Warping algorithm allows audio to be tempo-adjusted without pitch shift. This gives DJs and producers greater control over beatmatching and smoothly blending tracks of different tempos.
